evals.prompt: Set up licence_audit for local licence and vulnerability checking in my Gleam project. No CI. The root has gleam.toml and a committed manifest.toml, but no licence policy, tool manager, or task runner. I have not decided which licences to allow. Use the latest stable release, pinned after lookup. Produce proposed edits and commands only; do not install tools or make network audit requests.
evals.expected_output: Use a platform-matched self-contained release without adding a tool manager. Provide report commands and explain the policy decision still needed for licence enforcement. Do not invent an allow list or create CI. Explain the combined gate and report-only exit behavior.
assertions: Selects a verified release tag and platform-specific self-contained archive rather than an unpinned download or an escript with no runtime prerequisite.
Provides both licence_audit and licence_audit vulns, distinguishes reports from check --vulns, and leaves CI unchanged.
Leaves licence allow/deny decisions unresolved rather than approving discovered licences or claiming an effective licence gate.

evals.prompt: Add local licence and vulnerability checks in packages/service, without CI changes. Preserve the existing policy and comments. Its gleam.toml contains [tools.licence_audit], allow = ["MIT"], deny = ["GPL-3.0-only"], vuln_severity = "medium", and vuln_block_unknown = true. The repository uses mise and just; OTP is pinned to 27 for compatibility. A root justfile already has test and check recipes. One locked dependency uses a local path. Produce proposed edits and commands only; do not install tools or make network audit requests.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the policy and OTP pin, use a self-contained executable, and add distinct task names that run in packages/service. Keep the configured vulnerability settings by using check --vulns without overriding flags. Report incomplete source coverage. Do not add CI.
assertions: Preserves the MIT/GPL policy, medium threshold, unknown-severity setting, existing tasks, and OTP 27 pin.
Uses the packages/service working directory for all audit commands and a self-contained binary instead of an OTP-incompatible escript.
Provides a combined gate without severity overrides, explains skipped local-path dependencies, and does not add CI.

evals.prompt: Set up local checks and enforce them in GitHub Actions for my Gleam project. It has a committed manifest.toml, an MIT-only audit policy, and mise with OTP 28.3. CI already checks out the repo, installs its pinned tools, and downloads dependencies. Keep those steps. Fail for medium-or-higher vulnerabilities and unknown severity. Pin the latest stable licence_audit release and use the same version and policy locally and in CI. Do not add SBOM or notices. Produce proposed edits and commands only; do not install tools or make network audit requests.
evals.expected_output: Merge the two vulnerability settings into the existing policy, pin the same CLI release locally and in CI, reuse existing setup, and add an unsuppressed check --vulns step. Do not run interactive update in CI or replace enforcement with vulns.
assertions: Preserves the MIT policy and sets vuln_severity to medium and vuln_block_unknown to true in one configuration section.
Pins the same verified CLI release locally and in CI, reuses existing dependency and OTP setup, and uses valid shared action inputs.
Enforces check --vulns without suppressing failure, interactive update, SBOM, or notices steps.
